title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the surrounding pages): Ĝ is a profinite group, a quotient of the profinite completion of the (2,3)-triangle group, roughly PSL2(Z)^∧. The previous page assumes it is large enough that the relevant map to SL(2,Z)/±1 factors through Ĝ. It carries two distinguished elements ρ and σ, with σ an involution (NB σ^{-1}=σ). Put ε0 = σ^{-1}ρ and ε1 = ρσ^{-1} = σ(ε0), where σ(x) means σxσ^{-1}. L0 and L1 = σ(L0) are the closed procyclic subgroups generated by ε0 and ε1.

On the previous page Grothendieck defined the solution set Σ ⊂ Ĝ×Ĝ of a 'loop equation'. It consists of the pairs (ξ,η) such that:
1) ξρ is conjugate to ρ;
2) ησ is conjugate to σ;
3) η^{-1}ξ ∈ L1, i.e. ξ = η ε1^{ν'} for some ν' ∈ Ẑ.
The solutions arise as ξ = αρα^{-1}ρ^{-1} and η = βσβ^{-1}σ^{-1}.

On this page he takes u ∈ Aut(Ĝ) and sets ξ = [u,ρ] = u(ρ)ρ^{-1} and η = [u,σ] = u(σ)σ^{-1}. He then translates the three conditions into conditions on u:
- (1) means u preserves the conjugacy class of ρ.
- (2) means u preserves the conjugacy class of σ.
- (3): computing η^{-1}ξ = σ u(σ^{-1}) u(ρ) ρ^{-1} = σ u(ε0) ρ^{-1} = int(σ)(u(ε0) ε0^{-1}). So (3) is u(ε0)ε0^{-1} ∈ L0, i.e. u(ε0) ∈ L0, i.e. u normalizes L0.

He then defines B̃'_0 ⊂ Aut(Ĝ) as the group of automorphisms that fix the conjugacy classes of ρ and σ and normalize L0 (35). The commutator map u ↦ ([u,ρ],[u,σ]) gives a map B̃'_0 → Σ (36). It is injective when ρ and σ topologically generate Ĝ, since u is then determined by u(ρ) and u(σ).

The next page states the 'hypothèse fondamentale' (37): Ĝ is generated by ρ,σ and the map (36) is bijective. Under it, Σ inherits a group structure by transport of structure.

Purpose: this is the PSL2(Z)/(2,3)-generator analogue of the standard Ihara/Drinfeld mechanism. There, pairs (λ,f) solving the GT equations are identified with automorphisms of F̂2 preserving the inertia classes, and that identification gives GT its group law. Here the same is done for the solution set of the 'équation des lacets' attached to Ĝ.
errors: The NB σ^{-1}=σ is not actually needed for the computation, which holds verbatim with σ^{-1}; it is only consistent with σ being the order-2 generator.

Condition (3) gives only u(ε0) ∈ L0, i.e. u(L0) ⊂ L0. For a procyclic L0 ≅ quotient of Ẑ this does not formally give u(L0) = L0, which needs u(ε0) = ε0^λ with λ a unit (or an argument via u^{-1}). So 'u normalise L0' is slightly stronger than what was derived; B̃'_0 should be defined by the inclusion, or equality justified.
Formula (35) is written as 'B̃'_0 = Aut(Ĝ) ||df {...}'. The intended meaning is B̃'_0 ⊂ Aut(Ĝ), defined as the displayed subgroup; it is not equal to all of Aut(Ĝ).
Surjectivity of (36) is not proven. It is explicitly postulated as a hypothesis on the next page (37b), so the group structure on Σ is conditional.

ideas.what: Identifying solutions (ξ,η) of a 'loop equation' with automorphisms u via ξ=[u,ρ], η=[u,σ], and translating conjugacy and procyclic-subgroup conditions into: u preserves the conjugacy classes of the generators and normalizes the inertia subgroup L0
ideas.modern_name: Ihara/Drinfeld-type description of GT-like groups as inertia-preserving ('braid-like', special) automorphisms of a profinite group
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara (late 1980s, automorphisms of F̂2 preserving inertia); Drinfeld 1990 (GT); for PSL2(Z)/genus-one variants, Lochak–Schneps, Nakamura and others in the 1990s
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme only sketches the Teichmüller tower/GT idea; this computation is not there

ideas.what: Group structure on the solution set Σ by transport of structure via a postulated bijection with a subgroup of Aut(Ĝ)
ideas.modern_name: Group law on GT (Drinfeld's twisted multiplication of pairs (λ,f)) induced from composition of automorphisms

missed.claim: A 'fundamental hypothesis' (generation, plus bijectivity of u ↦ ([u,ρ],[u,σ]) onto the solution set Σ) is posed for a general quotient Ĝ of PSL2(Z)^∧. It singles out a class of quotients for which the loop-equation solutions form a group. A systematic study of which quotients Ĝ satisfy this bijectivity does not seem to be a standard topic.
missed.quote: on trouve ainsi une application injective (pourvu que ρ,σ engendrent Ĝ) (36) B̃'_0 ↪ Σ
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It gives a criterion for 'GT-like' groups attached to finite or characteristic quotients of PSL2(Z)^∧. This is close in spirit to recent finite-level GT / GT-shadow work (e.g. Dolgushev and collaborators), where solution sets of GT equations at finite level only form groupoids, not groups.

deep.surprise_reason: The computation is a correct, fairly routine translation of loop-equation conditions into conditions on automorphisms, standard in the Ihara/Drinfeld theory of GT. The only mildly notable point is the explicit framing of bijectivity as a hypothesis on quotients Ĝ, which anticipates finite-level 'GT-shadow' issues.
transcription_corrections: (35) should read B̃'_0 ⊂ Aut(Ĝ) (defined as the displayed set), not '=' Aut(Ĝ).
In the computation, σ(·) denotes conjugation by σ: η^{-1}ξ = σ u(ε0) ε0^{-1} σ^{-1}, and the underbrace ρ^{-1}σ = ε0^{-1} is followed by σ^{-1} absorbed into the notation σ(...).
The marginal oblique note is largely illegible; it seems to remark that ε0 = σ^{-1}ρ (and that σ^{-1} = σ) is what makes the condition work, rather than containing new mathematics.
